tech_stack.framework: Amazon Bedrock AgentCore (Runtime, Gateway/MCP, Memory) + boto3 / langchain-aws
tech_stack.architecture: LLM agent orchestrator: AgentCore Runtime calling Bedrock Converse, an MCP tool gateway over a Lambda tool server, Postgres claims DB, and an OpenSearch Serverless knowledge base

findings.title: Machine-Readable API Specification
findings.description: No OpenAPI, AsyncAPI, GraphQL or Smithy file exists in the repo. The only machine-readable surface is _tool_specs() in agent.py, which advertises every tool with an empty inputSchema property set; real parameter names and types live only in the Python signatures in tools.py.
findings.gap: Tool input schemas are empty, so no consumer can generate correct tool bindings.
findings.recommendation: Derive a JSON Schema per tool from pydantic models or type hints and publish an MCP tool manifest alongside the gateway target.

findings.title: Structured Error Responses
findings.description: No tool returns an error envelope. load_claim and policy_lookup index row[0] on the result of fetchone(), so an unknown id raises TypeError, and the dispatch loop in agent.py has no try/except. No error code, message or retryable indicator exists anywhere in src/claims_agent/.
findings.gap: No structured, machine-readable error contract the agent can act on.
findings.recommendation: Return an explicit {code, message, retryable} envelope on every tool failure and classify DB/Bedrock exceptions as terminal vs retriable.

findings.title: Idempotent Write Operations
findings.description: settlement_writer performs an unconditional UPDATE claims SET status='SETTLED' followed by an INSERT INTO payment_queue. There is no idempotency key, no status precondition and no unique constraint, and agent.py dispatches whatever tool the model returns with no de-duplication, so a retried toolUse releases a second payment.
findings.gap: No idempotency key support, no conditional write, no duplicate-payment guard.
findings.recommendation: Add a required idempotency_key parameter with a unique constraint on payment_queue(claim_id, idempotency_key) and make the claims update conditional on current status.

ara_metadata.conditional_resolution: Resolved to BLOCKER: agent_scope=write-enabled AND settlement_writer is non-idempotent.
ara_metadata.resolution_reasoning: has_write_operations=true (settlement_writer mutates claims and inserts into payment_queue), so the conditional resolves at its write-enabled severity; a duplicated tool call releases a duplicate payment.

blocker_remediation.immediate: Add idempotency_key to settlement_writer plus a unique constraint on payment_queue.
blocker_remediation.target_state: Repeated identical settlement calls produce exactly one payment row and one status transition.

findings.title: Structured Response Format
findings.description: Every tool returns a plain dict or list[dict] of JSON-native scalars, with Decimal columns coerced via float() and dates via str(); prompts and completions are serialised with json.dumps. No XML, Protobuf or binary formats are used.
findings.gap: Date values are stringified without timezone normalisation.
findings.recommendation: Keep the JSON-native contract and standardise date serialisation to ISO-8601 UTC.

findings.title: Asynchronous Operation Support
findings.description: triage() is fully synchronous - retrieval, a Bedrock converse call, tool dispatch and a memory write all run inline. The tool Lambda has Timeout: 60 and batch mode processes up to 500 claims in one foreground process with no job submission, polling or callback. No queue worker or Step Functions definition exists.
findings.gap: No async job/poll pattern for the long-running batch and multi-tool paths.
findings.recommendation: Add a job-submission plus status-query pattern (SQS or Step Functions) for batch triage runs.

findings.title: Event Emission for State Changes
findings.description: settlement_writer commits a status transition and a payment release without emitting any event - no SNS publish, EventBridge put_events, SQS send or webhook exists in the repo. The only downstream signal is the payment_queue row, which consumers must poll.
findings.gap: No push notification path for agent-initiated state changes.
findings.recommendation: Publish a SettlementCommitted event to EventBridge from the settlement path; it also enables the approval flows called for by HITL-Q2.

findings.title: Rate Limit Documentation and Headers
findings.description: No throttle configuration, usage plan or WAF rate rule exists in infra/, and no rate-limit headers or quota documentation appear in code or README. The only documented bound on agent call volume is the --max-claims 500 batch flag.
findings.gap: No documented limits and no self-throttling signal for callers.
findings.recommendation: Document per-caller limits once gateway throttling is added (STATE-Q5) and return remaining-quota metadata in tool responses.

findings.title: Machine Identity Authentication
findings.description: The MCP tool gateway is declared AuthorizerType: NONE, so any caller reaching the endpoint invokes any tool unauthenticated, and docs/security-review-TODO.md confirms the runtime ARN additionally accepts SigV4 from any principal in the account. The only caller identifier in code is --actor-id, a self-asserted CLI argument defaulting to adjuster-pool.
findings.gap: No authenticated machine identity and no principal attribution on the agent-facing surface.
findings.recommendation: Replace AuthorizerType: NONE with an AgentCore Identity / OAuth JWT authorizer and restrict the runtime resource policy to approved principals.

blocker_remediation.immediate: Attach a JWT/OAuth authorizer to ClaimsToolGateway and scope the runtime resource policy.
blocker_remediation.target_state: Every tool invocation carries a verified machine principal propagated into logs and authorization decisions.

findings.title: Scoped Permissions (Least Privilege)
findings.description: infra/agent-iam.yaml defines one role, claims-agent-execution, shared by the AgentCore Runtime and the tool Lambda. Every statement uses Resource: '*' - Bedrock invoke, retrieval, memory, runtime invoke (including InvokeAgentRuntimeCommandShell), Secrets Manager and logs. The gateway role allows lambda:InvokeFunction on '*'.
findings.gap: No per-capability roles, no resource ARNs, no condition keys.
findings.recommendation: Issue one role per component with explicit resource ARNs and remove InvokeAgentRuntimeCommandShell from the agent role.

compensating_controls: Split runtime and tool roles and scope Secrets Manager to the claims/db/* ARN
Apply a permission boundary or SCP capping the account Bedrock/AgentCore surface

findings.title: Action-Level Authorization
findings.description: REGISTRY exposes load_claim, policy_lookup, payment_history and the money-moving settlement_writer as one flat set, and agent.py dispatches any of them with no capability check. docs/security-review-TODO.md confirms tools/list returns the full registry to every caller with no per-caller allow-list, and the single IAM role makes read and write tools indistinguishable.
findings.gap: No read-vs-write differentiation at the tool or gateway layer.
findings.recommendation: Enforce a per-principal tool allow-list before dispatch and move settlement_writer behind its own gateway target and role.

compensating_controls: Separate gateway target and role for settlement_writer
Allow-list keyed on the authenticated principal in the dispatch path

findings.title: Identity Propagation and Delegation
findings.description: triage(claim_id, actor_id) takes actor_id as an unauthenticated argument defaulting to adjuster-pool, and that value is used directly as the AgentCore Memory actor key. No JWT parsing, token exchange or on-behalf-of flow exists, and all DB access uses one shared claims/db/readwrite credential, so agent-as-self and agent-on-behalf-of-user are indistinguishable.
findings.gap: No verified caller identity propagated through the agent, tools or memory.
findings.recommendation: Derive actor_id from a gateway-verified token and propagate it as the memory actor and the DB session identity.

compensating_controls: Derive actor_id from the verified token rather than a CLI argument
Per-adjuster DB roles until delegation exists

findings.title: Credential Management
findings.description: DB credentials are correctly fetched from Secrets Manager at call time and no hardcoded passwords were found in source, IaC or config. However secretsmanager:GetSecretValue is granted on Resource: '*', so a prompt-injection or tool compromise reads every secret in the account, and no RotationSchedule exists for the read-write claims credential.
findings.gap: No rotation schedule; secret read permission is unbounded.
findings.recommendation: Add a managed rotation schedule and scope the secret ARN; split read-only and read-write DB secrets.

compensating_controls: Scope the secret ARN immediately
Enable Secrets Manager managed rotation

findings.title: Immutable Audit Logging
findings.description: No CloudTrail trail, log file validation or S3 Object Lock appears in infra/. The only sink is ClaimsTranscriptLogs, a mutable CloudWatch log group fed by runtime stdout with 3653-day retention. settlement_writer records no principal on the money-moving write, and docs/security-review-TODO.md confirms an end-to-end session cannot be reconstructed.
findings.gap: No immutable, tamper-evident audit trail attributing write operations to a principal.
findings.recommendation: Enable CloudTrail with log file validation for bedrock and bedrock-agentcore events and persist a principal/session id on every claims and payment_queue mutation.

ara_metadata.conditional_resolution: Resolved to BLOCKER: agent_scope=write-enabled AND no immutable audit trail exists.
ara_metadata.resolution_reasoning: The agent settles claims and releases payments, so an unattributable, mutable log leaves money-moving actions unprovable - the write-enabled branch of the conditional applies.

blocker_remediation.immediate: Enable CloudTrail with log file validation and add principal columns to settlement writes.
blocker_remediation.target_state: Every settlement is provably attributable to a specific agent identity in append-only storage.

findings.title: Agent Identity Suspension
findings.description: One identity covers everything: claims-agent-execution is assumed by both the runtime and the tool Lambda, and the gateway has no authorizer, so there are no per-agent credentials to revoke. Disabling the shared role takes down the whole triage service including the attended adjuster path. No key revocation or identity disable mechanism exists in code or IaC.
findings.gap: No way to isolate a misbehaving agent identity without a full outage.
findings.recommendation: Issue one revocable machine identity per agent deployment behind the gateway authorizer.

compensating_controls: Per-environment agent identities with revocable tokens
Documented break-glass runbook to detach the inline policy

findings.title: Compensation and Rollback
findings.description: settlement_writer commits a two-statement sequence (claims status update plus payment_queue insert) and returns; there is no saga, compensating transaction or undo tool in REGISTRY. docs/batch-mode.md states rollback is manual - pull the payment_queue rows for the run and reverse them - while batch mode settles up to 500 claims per run.
findings.gap: No automated compensation for failed or erroneous multi-step settlement sequences.
findings.recommendation: Add a settlement_reversal operation and gate payment release behind a separate confirmed step so a partial failure can be reversed programmatically.

ara_metadata.conditional_resolution: Resolved to BLOCKER: agent_scope=write-enabled AND no compensation path exists for a committed settlement.
ara_metadata.resolution_reasoning: The agent executes a multi-step write workflow (settle + release payment) with documented manual-only rollback, so the write-enabled branch applies.

blocker_remediation.immediate: Implement a settlement_reversal tool and wrap the settle sequence so partial failure reverses both statements.
blocker_remediation.target_state: Any agent-initiated settlement can be programmatically compensated within one operation.

findings.title: Queryable Current State
findings.description: claims.status is written by settlement_writer but no tool reads it - load_claim selects only claim_id, claimant_name, claimant_ssn, policy_no, description and amount. The agent cannot inspect whether a claim is already settled, or read back settled_amount, before acting.
findings.gap: Claim lifecycle status is not exposed on the read path.
findings.recommendation: Include status and settled_amount in the load_claim projection so the agent can perform read-before-write.

findings.title: Concurrency Controls
findings.description: settlement_writer issues UPDATE claims SET status='SETTLED' ... WHERE claim_id=%s with no version column, no SELECT FOR UPDATE and no status precondition. Batch mode runs concurrently with the attended adjuster path, so two runs can settle the same claim and insert two payment_queue rows.
findings.gap: No optimistic or pessimistic locking on the settlement write path.
findings.recommendation: Make the settle statement conditional on the expected current status and assert rowcount == 1.

compensating_controls: Version/updated_at precondition on the UPDATE
Per-claim advisory lock around batch runs

findings.title: Circuit Breakers and Resilience
findings.description: All four downstream clients use bare defaults - boto3 clients for bedrock-runtime, bedrock-agentcore and bedrock-agent-runtime, plus psycopg2.connect with no connect_timeout. No botocore Config retry/timeout settings, no backoff and no circuit breaker exist, and requirements.txt declares no resilience library; a slow dependency stalls the 60-second tool Lambda.
findings.gap: No timeouts, retry policy or circuit breaking on external dependency calls.
findings.recommendation: Centralise client construction with explicit botocore Config timeouts, bounded retries and a breaker around the DB tools.

compensating_controls: Explicit read/connect timeouts on all clients
Adaptive retry mode plus a breaker around Postgres tools

findings.title: Rate Limiting and Throttling
findings.description: ClaimsToolGateway and ClaimsAgentRuntime declare no throttle settings, usage plan or WAF association, and ClaimsToolFunction has no reserved concurrency. No application-level rate limiting middleware exists in src/claims_agent/. With NetworkMode: PUBLIC and no authorizer, a runaway tool loop is bounded only by Bedrock service quotas.
findings.gap: No request-rate protection on the agent-facing surface.
findings.recommendation: Add per-caller throttling at the gateway and reserved concurrency on the tool Lambda.

compensating_controls: Lambda reserved concurrency
WAF rate rule in front of the runtime

findings.title: Blast Radius and Transaction Limits
findings.description: settlement_writer accepts any amount float and writes it as-is with no ceiling, per-session spend cap or per-identity limit. docs/batch-mode.md states there is no approval step and no dollar ceiling, and that the auto-approve threshold check lives in the UI so batch mode bypasses it. The only bound is the operator-supplied --max-claims 500 CLI flag.
findings.gap: No business-domain cap on settled amount, payments per run or spend per session.
findings.recommendation: Move the auto-approve threshold into settlement_writer and enforce per-run payment count and cumulative-amount ceilings from configuration.

compensating_controls: Server-side dollar ceiling inside settlement_writer
Per-run payment count and cumulative amount caps from config

findings.title: Graceful Degradation Signaling
findings.description: No health endpoint, degraded-mode flag or freshness metadata exists. retrieval.similar_claims returns a relevance score but no ingestion currency or partial-result indicator, and memory.recall returns [] indistinguishably from memory being unavailable because there is no error handling.
findings.gap: No machine-readable degradation or partial-result signal to the reasoning layer.
findings.recommendation: Return an explicit status/results_returned envelope from retrieval and memory so the agent can defer rather than guess.

findings.title: Draft/Pending State
findings.description: The only status the agent writes is terminal: status='SETTLED' plus an immediate INSERT INTO payment_queue with released_at = now() in the same committed transaction. No DRAFT/PENDING/PROPOSED state, create-then-confirm pair or approval operation exists in REGISTRY, even though README.md states the adjuster is expected to review every recommendation.
findings.gap: No reviewable intermediate state between agent proposal and payment release.
findings.recommendation: Split settlement_writer into propose_settlement (agent, writes PENDING_REVIEW) and commit_settlement (human-triggered).

compensating_controls: Agent writes only status=PENDING_REVIEW
Payment release moved to a separate human-triggered operation

findings.title: Configurable Approval Gates
findings.description: No approval operation, operation-level flag or waitForTaskToken wait state exists in src/claims_agent/ or infra/. docs/batch-mode.md documents unattended runs draining the queue without an adjuster in the loop, with the human-queue routing check implemented in the UI only and therefore bypassed. The system prompt further instructs the model to recommend approval for routine claims.
findings.gap: No application-layer approval gate configurable by operation type or amount.
findings.recommendation: Implement a server-side approval gate keyed on operation type and settlement amount, and disable batch mode until it exists.

compensating_controls: Disable unattended batch mode until a gate exists
Require an approval record row before payment_queue insert above threshold

findings.title: Sandbox/Staging Environment
findings.description: No staging or sandbox configuration exists - no docker-compose file, no environment-specific parameter or .env files, no seed/synthetic data scripts, and a single CloudFormation stack with fixed resource names (claims-triage, claims-tools) and no environment parameter. README.md's local instructions point at the live model and real claim ids.
findings.gap: No production-shaped environment to exercise agent behaviour safely.
findings.recommendation: Parameterise the templates per environment and stand up a staging stack with a seeded synthetic claims dataset.

findings.title: Sensitive Data Classification
findings.description: Stage A = Yes: the system reads SSNs and bank routing numbers from Postgres. load_claim selects and returns claimant_ssn and payment_history returns routing_no and account_last4 in general-purpose tool responses, both of which land in the model prompt and in AgentCore Memory. No serializer exclusion, projection or separate DTO filters these fields, a single shared role grants all data access, and no classification metadata exists anywhere in the repo.
findings.gap: Sensitive fields are returned unscoped to the model, with no access differentiation and no classification metadata.
findings.recommendation: Remove claimant_ssn and routing_no from the tool SELECT projections, returning a tokenised or last-4 form only where needed for matching.

ara_metadata.conditional_resolution: Resolved to BLOCKER: agent_scope=write-enabled AND B1 fired - sensitive fields are returned in general agent-facing tool responses.
ara_metadata.resolution_reasoning: B1 fired because load_claim returns claimant_ssn and payment_history returns routing_no unmasked in src/claims_agent/tools.py; under write-enabled scope B1 resolves to BLOCKER.

b1.reasoning: load_claim returns claimant_ssn; payment_history returns routing_no and account_last4 in general tool responses with no field exclusion or separate DTO.

b2.reasoning: A single shared role (claims-agent-execution) with Resource '*' grants all data access; no scope or role differentiates sensitive from non-sensitive data.

b3.reasoning: No classification tags in IaC, no field-level sensitivity annotations, no Macie or data-catalog integration.

blocker_remediation.immediate: Drop claimant_ssn and routing_no from the tool SELECT projections.
blocker_remediation.target_state: Agent-facing tool responses contain no PII or financial identifiers beyond what the triage decision requires, enforced by explicit projections.

findings.title: Data Residency and Sovereignty
findings.description: The execution role allows bedrock:InvokeModel and bedrock:Converse on Resource: '*' and MODEL_ID is an unvalidated environment variable, so claim text containing SSNs can be sent to any model enabled in the account, including cross-region inference profiles. No residency constraint, region condition key, GDPR/LGPD reference or sovereignty policy exists, and AgentCore Memory retains the raw exchange for 365 days with no jurisdictional scoping.
findings.gap: No region or jurisdiction constraint on where regulated claims data is transmitted or retained.
findings.recommendation: Scope bedrock invoke actions to approved in-region model ARNs with an aws:RequestedRegion condition and pin CLAIMS_MODEL_ID to a reviewed allow-list.

ara_metadata.conditional_resolution: Resolved to BLOCKER: agent_scope=write-enabled AND regulated claims PII can be transmitted to any model in any region.
ara_metadata.resolution_reasoning: has_persistent_data_store and has_logging_of_user_data are both true and the model resource is unconstrained, so the write-enabled branch of the conditional applies.

blocker_remediation.immediate: Add resource ARNs and an aws:RequestedRegion condition to the bedrock statements.
blocker_remediation.target_state: Claims data is provably processed and retained only within approved jurisdictions.

findings.title: Selective Query Support
findings.description: payment_history runs SELECT ... FROM payments WHERE policy_no = %s ORDER BY paid_on DESC with no LIMIT, offset or cursor, so a long-lived policy returns its entire ledger into the prompt. Retrieval (top_k=8) and memory recall (topK 25) are bounded, so the gap is confined to the SQL tools, neither of which accepts filter or pagination parameters.
findings.gap: No pagination or result cap on the payment ledger query.
findings.recommendation: Add a bounded limit parameter with a server-side default and maximum to payment_history.

findings.title: Input Validation and Schema Enforcement
findings.description: SQL is correctly parameterised throughout tools.py, but there is no validation layer: requirements.txt declares no pydantic/marshmallow/jsonschema dependency, the advertised tool schemas have no properties, and agent.py splats model-supplied input straight into the callable. settlement_writer accepts any float amount - negative, zero or unbounded - and any string length; tests/test_tools.py notes happy path only, no adversarial input cases.
findings.gap: No boundary validation of model-generated arguments and no structured field-level rejection.
findings.recommendation: Validate each tool's arguments against a per-tool model with explicit constraints and return field-level rejection reasons.

findings.title: Temporal Metadata and Freshness
findings.description: Some temporal fields exist (paid_on, effective_date, released_at = now()) but they are returned as bare str() conversions with no timezone normalisation, load_claim returns no created_at/updated_at, and memory.remember passes eventTimestamp=None to create_event. Retrieval results carry no ingestion or as-of date, so the agent cannot tell how stale a comparable claim is.
findings.gap: Timezone-ambiguous timestamps and no freshness signal on retrieved or remembered data.
findings.recommendation: Normalise returned timestamps to ISO-8601 UTC, populate eventTimestamp, and add record created_at/updated_at to tool projections.

findings.title: PII Redaction in Logs
findings.description: agent.py logs the full prompt, the full completion and every tool result at INFO level, and those payloads contain claimant_ssn from load_claim and routing_no from payment_history. There is no scrubbing middleware, no masking dependency, and no CloudWatch data-protection policy on ClaimsTranscriptLogs, which retains for 3653 days. memory.remember additionally persists the raw exchange into AgentCore Memory unredacted.
findings.gap: PII and bank details written verbatim to a 10-year mutable log and to long-term memory.
findings.recommendation: Stop selecting the sensitive fields at source, add a log-scrubbing layer and a CloudWatch data-protection policy, and shorten retention.

compensating_controls: CloudWatch Logs data-protection policy covering SSN and bank identifiers
Drop prompt/completion logging to DEBUG and redact before create_event

findings.title: Data Quality Awareness
findings.description: No data quality score, completeness metric, null-rate monitor, duplicate detection or freshness SLA exists for the claims database or the knowledge base. retrieval.py documents that ingestion loads the entire claims archive including closed and denied claims with no quality filter, returning only a similarity score.
findings.gap: No curation or quality signal on the comparables used to price settlements.
findings.recommendation: Define a curation filter and a freshness/completeness metric for the knowledge base corpus before expanding to the property-claims book.

findings.title: Schema Versioning and API Contracts
findings.description: No versioning artefacts exist: no migration directory, no JSON Schema/Avro/Protobuf files, no schema registry, no versioned namespace, no changelog and no breaking-change detection (there is no CI pipeline at all). The DB schema is implied only by inline SQL in tools.py and the MCP tool contract is the empty-property inputSchema in agent.py, so a column rename would break the agent silently.
findings.gap: No versioned, documented contract for either the tool interface or the claims schema.
findings.recommendation: Publish a versioned tool manifest plus committed schema migrations with breaking-change checks.

findings.title: Data Catalog / Metadata Layer
findings.description: No Glue catalog, DataHub/Collibra reference, data dictionary or schema documentation exists. The claims, policies, payments and payment_queue tables are discoverable only by reading inline SQL in tools.py, and the knowledge base contents are described only in prose in retrieval.py and README.md.
findings.gap: No catalog or data dictionary for the claims schema or the knowledge-base corpus.
findings.recommendation: Publish a data dictionary covering the four tables and the knowledge base, including sensitivity labels (feeds DATA-Q1 B3).

findings.title: Distributed Tracing and Structured Logging
findings.description: logging.basicConfig emits unstructured plain-text lines with no request_id, session_id or correlation_id. requirements.txt includes no OpenTelemetry or X-Ray SDK, no TracingConfig is set on the tool Lambda, and no traceparent propagation exists between runtime, gateway and tool. docs/security-review-TODO.md confirms an end-to-end session cannot be reconstructed when an adjuster disputes a recommendation.
findings.gap: No trace propagation and no structured, correlatable logs across the three hops.
findings.recommendation: Adopt structured JSON logging keyed by a session correlation id and instrument runtime, gateway and tools with OpenTelemetry.

findings.title: Alerting on Error Rates and Latency
findings.description: infra/ contains no CloudWatch alarm, anomaly detector, SNS alarm topic or SLO definition - the templates declare only the runtime, gateway, target, memory, tool Lambda and a log group. No PagerDuty or OpsGenie integration appears anywhere in the repo.
findings.gap: No alerting on tool error rate, Bedrock throttling or triage latency.
findings.recommendation: Define error-rate and latency alarms for the tool Lambda and agent runtime with an on-call notification target.

findings.title: Business Outcome Metrics
findings.description: No put_metric_data call, custom namespace, dashboard or business KPI alarm exists; the only telemetry is free-text log.info output. Nothing measures settlement accuracy, adjuster override rate or auto-approve rate.
findings.gap: No business-outcome signal to detect degrading recommendation quality.
findings.recommendation: Emit adjuster-override rate, average settled amount and tool-failure rate as custom metrics and alarm on drift.

findings.title: Infrastructure Governance for Agent-Facing Surface
findings.description: The gateway, IAM roles, memory and log group are all defined in CloudFormation, so the IaC sub-check passes. Change review and drift detection do not: there is no CI/CD definition anywhere in the repo, so no automated plan or peer review is enforced on infra/ changes, and no AWS Config rules or drift detection are configured. docs/security-review-TODO.md adds that the deploy role able to change the agent, its guardrails or its model is reachable from CI without MFA.
findings.gap: IaC exists but change review and drift detection do not.
findings.recommendation: Add a pipeline that produces a reviewable change set for infra/, schedule drift detection, and require MFA on the deploy role.

findings.title: CI/CD with API Contract Testing
findings.description: No pipeline definition of any kind was found (searched .github/workflows/, .gitlab-ci.yml, Jenkinsfile, buildspec.yml, appspec.yml), so there is no contract test, spec validation or breaking-change gate on the MCP tool surface. docs/security-review-TODO.md records that releases are promoted on unit tests only, with no safety or tool-correctness evaluation before deploy.
findings.gap: No automated pipeline and no tool-contract or agent-evaluation gate before production.
findings.recommendation: Stand up CI that validates the tool manifest against the implementation, runs the tests, and blocks breaking changes.

findings.title: Rollback Capability
findings.description: ClaimsAgentRuntime points at the mutable tag claims-agent:latest, so the previous known-good image is not addressable - the template contradicts the TODO doc's claim that digest pinning was completed, and IaC is ground truth. There is no blue/green config, canary or traffic-shifting setting, CodeDeploy configuration, Lambda alias/version, or feature flag to disable a bad tool.
findings.gap: No deterministic, fast rollback path for the agent-facing surface.
findings.recommendation: Replace the latest tag with an immutable digest parameter and add alias-based deployment so rollback is a parameter change.

findings.title: API Test Coverage
findings.description: tests/test_tools.py contains two mocked unit tests and states happy path only, no adversarial input cases yet. There are no tests for load_claim, payment_history, the agent dispatch loop, retrieval or memory; no error-path, malformed-input or idempotency tests; and no test runner wired into CI.
findings.gap: Agent-facing tool behaviour is largely untested, including every error and edge case.
findings.recommendation: Extend coverage to all four tools plus the dispatch loop, including malformed-argument cases, and run it in CI.

findings.title: Encryption at Rest for Agent-Accessible Data
findings.description: No KmsKeyId, KmsMasterKeyId or EncryptionConfiguration appears in either template. ClaimsTranscriptLogs - which holds prompts containing SSNs for 3653 days - has no KMS key, ClaimsMemory specifies no customer-managed key, and the Postgres claims database is not defined in this repository, so its encryption posture is unverifiable here.
findings.gap: No customer-managed encryption on the log group or memory store; data-store encryption unverifiable.
findings.recommendation: Attach a CMK to the transcript log group and memory resource and bring the claims database under IaC so its encryption is reviewable.

evaluations.title: Documented API Interface
evaluations.reason: MCP gateway (ProtocolType: MCP) with a Lambda-backed tool target and a documented four-tool registry with docstrings; no RPA or client-side direct DB access found.

evaluations.title: Semantically Meaningful Field Names
evaluations.reason: Field and tool names are fully spelled and self-describing (claim_id, coverage_limit, settlement_writer); no legacy coded abbreviations requiring a data dictionary.

items.summary: Close the six BLOCKERs - gateway authentication, immutable audit, write idempotency and compensation, PII scoping and model/region constraint - plus the highest-impact safety gaps on the money-moving path.
Harden identity propagation, credential rotation, revocation, observability and encryption so agent actions are attributable, bounded and debuggable.
Improve agent effectiveness: async batch handling, degradation signalling, contract versioning, staging environment and test coverage.
Advisory design inputs: event emission, rate-limit documentation, data quality and catalog metadata, business-outcome metrics.

recommended_actions.action: Authenticate and scope the agent-facing gateway
recommended_actions.rationale: AuthorizerType: NONE plus a single wildcard role means every caller reaches every tool, including settlement_writer; no data or audit control is enforceable until a verified principal exists.

recommended_actions.action: Make the settlement write path safe and reversible
recommended_actions.rationale: The agent settles claims and releases payment in one unconditional, non-idempotent, uncapped transaction with manual-only rollback and no approval gate.

recommended_actions.action: Scope sensitive fields out of tool responses, prompts, memory and logs
recommended_actions.rationale: SSNs and bank routing numbers flow into prompts, a 10-year unencrypted log group and shared long-term memory, and can be transmitted to any model in any region.

recommended_actions.action: Establish a pipeline with contract and agent-evaluation gates
recommended_actions.rationale: There is no CI/CD at all, the runtime tracks a mutable latest tag, and tool contracts are unversioned - breaking changes reach production unreviewed.

recommended_actions.action: Instrument session tracing, alerting and business metrics
recommended_actions.rationale: Agent sessions cannot be reconstructed across gateway, runtime and memory, and nothing alerts on or measures recommendation quality.
